These are great for using your own coffee grounds! - I actually bought the perfect Pod EZ cup after getting this one, but was disappointed in that it was all plastic. Then I had the idea to use the filters that came with the Perfect Pod EZ cup on my Perfect Pod ECO-FLO. It's stainless steel (just a small amt of plastic in the lid only) and it works just as well in the ECO-FLO cup as it does in the plastic EZ cup. I switch back and forth between using my own coffee grounds and the decaff, organic compostable pods, which I love because they are so convenient to just pop into the Keurig, no mess, no cleanup. Just pitch in the trash when done! Now, the nice thing about using the filters in my stainless steel ECO-FLO Perfect Pod cup is that you just put about 2 teaspoons of coffee in them (more if you like stronger coffee or use less water for stronger coffee). Then you put the lid on, brew the coffee. Let the pod cool a bit and remove it. Pop off the lid and you will pull out the filter, which by this time, has formed it's own little one-piece barrel-shaped coffee pod that you just pitch in the trash. The filter lid actually sticks to the rest of the pod, so it really is like a one piece! No mess, no grounds to clean up or rinse out. Convenient as can be! Love it! This makes using my own coffee grounds in my mini-Keurig a much more attractive option than before, when I had to knock the coffee grounds out of the k-cup or fish them out, or rinse them out in the sink. Sometimes I ended up with coffee grounds everywhere! Well, NO more, problem solved!

Don't Fall For Its Good Looks. - Dumb me. I ignored a terrible review about the Kitchenaid Glass Cooktop Oven because the other posts were positive. The reviewer's negative headline had read in part "I HATE THIS OVEN". A little late now, but Ditto for me a million times over. There is no way any human can clean this particular black glass cooktop and have it look as it should. Scrub scrub scrub. Rinse, rinse, rinse. Dry dry, dry. And then some! ( Altho you're not supposed to, i have even resorted to a razor blade.) Others in my family have also tried cleaning this top. . A miserable experience each and every time! I cant even boil water without the droplets leaving a mess taking "1/2 day" ( Well , way too long and with too much effort) for it to look clean, shiny and smear- less again. I have had at least 12 ovens of all types throughout almost 40 years of cooking and re- locations. I fell in love with this one because i really loved its clean, sleek looks . Two of my children also have black glass cooktops. They assured me that keeping the black glass top clean was a cinch. It never dawned on me that their different brands would make such a huge difference. Soooo, I try my best to use the cooktop as infrequently as possible, as well as to keep the overhead lights low in that area. What a way to live especially for someone who has always enjoyed cooking. Now after maybe 6 months of constant agitation, Im more than ready to throw it in the trash. In fairness tho, it cooks fine. That's as it should be of course . Maybe i should just throw a towel over its ugly head .

Good replacement - will know more when break open after its used - The product is a direct replacement for my Kenmore (Lg) refrigerator. I broke the kenmore filter in half to determine its construction. It is a compressed tube of powdered activated carbon. The activated carbon filter does not appear sufficient to remove chlorinated organics ( suspect carcinogen occasionally found in water where organics combine with chlorine disinfectant at the water plant). It would act to filter particles and would act to remove chlorine ( normal disinfectant found in drinking water) It might also help with some taste or odor (adsorption by the activated carbon) I assume this filter has the same internals. Flow rate is a bit higher which could be from a less compact carbon tube or because the old filter was blocked by turbidity or particles in the water. I will follow up when this filter is used. For now it seems comparable to the original filter

Received as a gift - love these, now I can use my own roast in my Nespresso - I received a set of these reusable capsules as a gift from my wife. I have been roasting my own coffee for a few years now and always wanted to use my own coffee with our Nespresso machine.

I am glad that she bought them for me! The capsules are made of metal, and seem strong and solid. The set also comes with the rubber gasket, coffee scooper/tamper, and one-time use foil seals.

Using the capsule is pretty straightforward. I was able to achieve the best results when I filled the capsule completely full of grinds and tamped VERY firmly using the supplied tamper. Then all you have to do is place the rubber gasket over the top and affix one of the one-time use seals. It did take me a few shots to determine the correct grind size using my Krups grinder, but once I figured that out (trial and error) - everything was golden.

I have forgotten about my capsule a few times and almost threw it away! So, my advice is just make sure you remember to check your capsule discard tray. You could remove the capsule immediately after use - however since it is metal it gets really hot and can be a little uncomfortable to handle immediately after brewing. Also, the little rubber gasket can easily get lost when cleaning - so be diligent!

After some tweaking, fantastic coffee! - Obviously, reviews on this are generally positive, but I'm the guy who checks out a product like this by searching "Ekobrew sucks", so I read through the negative reviews first. I ended up getting two of these anyway based on the rest of the reviews, and now that I've used them for a while, I'm really surprised at some of the negative responses and the difficulties they've had. The gasket on the lid is excellent, and I've not once had a leaking or overflow problem. Usually I would think that would be an issue of using grounds that are too fine and water not getting through. However, I use a Cuisinart burr grinder and grind on the next-to-finest grind, and fill it to the line and tap it down (tap, like on the table, not tamp, like with my fingers), and get a beautiful dark stream of coffee coming out, and I've never had it overflow once, so I wonder if others have been packing their coffee tight. Now, it does take longer for all the water to get through than it does for a regular k-cup, but that's a negligible issue. Best bet is to use a variable grinder like that and experiment a little with the grind size until your coffee comes out how you like it. I've found a medium/drip grind gives you five scoop Maxwell House, fine grind gives you French press. Yes, I do find more coffee solids on the bottom of my cup afterward, and I guess if you don't like that you'll have issues with this. If you are an espresso or French press lover, though, you're getting exactly what you like - dark coffee, nice brown crema, and yes, just a bit of coffee solids at the finish.

For clean up, do rinse these right away. If you let them sit and dry, it does take a little extra effort, but if you pull it out and rinse it right away, it cleans out quickly.

All in all, well worth both the savings, AND you get to use the coffee that you've always liked.

Easy Way to Avoid an Opened Fridge - This is a nice and easy solution to prevent leaving your refrigerator or freezer opened accidentally. The package comes with two alarms with batteries already installed. You just have to attach the adhesives, pull out the plastic tabs on the batteries, and stick it to your fridge. When installing, make sure the gap between the two pieces are not too far apart or it will trigger a false alarm. Ours ended up sticking out a bit as you can see from our photos. The alarm itself is fairly loud, not mind numbingly loud, but loud enough for us to hear from two rooms away on a quiet day.

I tested both the vertical and this horizontal Doumigo induction cooktop - And this one is the one for me. I'm shorter and the vertical style caused a bit of an issue for me to reach the back burner easily. Other than that, this horizontal one is great! I hate using the old electric coil burners on my stove - I hate that the coils take forever to cool off so I set this unit on top of my old range, plugged it in (have an outlet next to the stove) and it was all over - no more using that stupid range! I live alone so I very seldom have more than two things cooking at the same time. Most often it would be to make something like a grilled cheese sandwich while heating up soup to go with the sandwich or something similar. The smooth surface is really easy to clean and the flat controls are very touch sensitive. I am seriously thinking of having my regular old stove removed and replace the space with just this dual induction cooktop. I happen to have a multi-use large microwave that allows me to air fry and bake along with microwaving, so that big electric range is just taking up space in my smaller kitchen. One thing I did do was find a silicone mat that fits the top of this cooktop so I can safety place items on the cooktop when not in use. I really do like this horizontal induction cooktop.
